headline: A preprint reports a cross-family pain-related activation direction and harmful choices under direct steering
summary: The v2 preprint reports a pain-related activation direction in 25 dense open-weight models across five families and 2B–72B parameters. In direct-steering experiments on fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 models, the authors report increased selection of harmful options over matched alternatives in most tested comparisons. They added random- and sadness-vector sham controls and concluded that repeated choices tracked whether steering remained active, not whether relief occurred; the first-choice pain-over-random difference on harm options remained. An independent team reports reproducing all 51 published table cells from original logs, meeting its fresh-run criterion on 14 of 15 checked cells, and finding a similar steering-schedule effect in a yoked control. These reports do not establish that the model sought relief or experienced pain. The results remain author-reported or independently reported, narrow to fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 forced-choice tasks, and do not show natural or deployed behavior.
